articleTitle: Use of ethnography to acquire an insider's view of engineering design teams
publicationTitle: Workshop on Soft Approaches to Product Introduction Improvement (Ref. No: 1997/342)
abstract: This paper is based on the findings of an EPSRC funded research project which has carried out longitudinal ethnographic studies of engineering design teams in the electronics industry. The first aim of the project was to improve the understanding of the tacit social processes which enable design teams to work effectively. The second aim was to use such understanding in the analysis and design of a socio-technical system to support the work of design teams. In this way the work has been conducted very much from the pragmatic perspective of human-centred systems design rather than the disinterested perspective of the anthropologist. The aim of this paper is to indicate the nature of the contribution made by a longitudinal ethnographic study to the design of the socio-technical system within which engineering design teams work.

articleTitle: Techniques to support strategic business change
publicationTitle: Workshop on Soft Approaches to Product Introduction Improvement (Ref. No: 1997/342)
abstract: This paper is concerned with analysing some "soft" methods and tools that have been used as part of a toolset to help small to medium sized manufacturing enterprises develop a better understanding of their business and hence to develop better business strategies as a result. The paper is separated into two parts. The first outlines the problem domain and additionally defines what is meant by "soft" in many of the approaches taken to support this domain. The second provides a brief description of a selection of the methods and supporting tools which have been applied as part of the toolset. The tools and methods described have been developed as part of an EPSRC research grant awarded to the MSI Research Institute at Loughborough University, UK.

articleTitle: Pragmatic models of concurrent product/process development
publicationTitle: Workshop on Soft Approaches to Product Introduction Improvement (Ref. No: 1997/342)
abstract: The research reported on in this paper is the result of a joint project between Hull and Cranfield Universities (UK). The research is funded by EPSRC and is in collaboration with Matra BAe Dynamics, Lucas Varity and Cirrus Technologies. The brief was to develop a technique that would enable an organisation to more accurately represent the product introduction process and to support this representation with evidence that could be readily understood by all involved in the process. A technique called pragmatic modelling has emerged from the research. This is a technique, grounded in ethnography, that aims to expose the social restrictions imposed on a process. Application of the technique is embodied in a methodology contained within a workbook. Use of the workbook will facilitate the generation of pragmatic models and hence support incremental improvement.

articleTitle: Soft systems methodology applied to PIP improvement
publicationTitle: Workshop on Soft Approaches to Product Introduction Improvement (Ref. No: 1997/342)
abstract: Summary form only given. In this paper, the authors report on the application of a soft systems methodology (SSM) to improvement in the product introduction process (PIP) for integrated aerospace manufacture. They briefly allude to the Boardman SSM and illustrate its application to this particular process. They conclude by remarking on the value of a soft systems approach to PIP improvement and discuss the requirements for users who may wish to consider adopting such an approach.
